1.text: There is no particular difference between the clothes of Reindeer and

2.text: those of Maritime Chukchee, except that the former use better reindeer-skins,

3.text: while the latter use seal-skins more frequently. Skins of reindeer-fawns are

4.text: highly prized as material for clothing, because they are very warm and at the

5.text: same time so light that a man clad in double garments is able to bustle

6.text: around in the open quite freely. When Middendorff¹ says that in his opinion

7.text: a good sheep-skin coat is to be preferred for travel, it may be ascribed to

8.text: the fact that he travelled only with the Tungus. The latter select for clothing

9.text: either the thinnest summer skins for making their holiday garments, or the

10.text: heaviest winter skins for making short overcoats, which are put on over the

11.text: usual clothes for riding-trips in the middle of winter. Moreover, the Tungus

12.text: usually have only small herds of reindeer, and cannot very well choose their

13.text: time for slaughtering or pick those animals whose skins are best fitted for

14.text: clothing, as the wealthy reindeer-breeders of the extreme northeast do. Skins

15.text: of the wolf, and perhaps also those of the wild sheep, surpass those of the

16.text: reindeer in their wearing and protecting qualities, but both are too rare to be

17.text: used regularly as material for clothing.

18.text: The Maritime people in these regions, unlike the American Eskimo, use

19.text: seal-skin but little for coats. This is because seal gives but slight protection

20.text: against the cold, while, on the other hand, it brings a much better price in

21.text: exchange for reindeer-skins. For this reason we find that only reindeer-skin

22.text: is used for winter coats. Seal-skin is more useful for trousers, because it

23.text: wears better, especially in the damp weather of spring. For spring and summer

24.text: boots, seal-skin is most serviceable. It is tough, wears extremely well, and

25.text: affords better protection against dampness and water than any other hide known

32.text: WINTER CLOTHING FOR MEN. — The style of clothes used by Chukchee

33.text: and Koryak men in winter is admirably adapted to its purpose. It therefore

34.text: prevails among most of the tribes of northeastern Asia, including the Russians.
